title: Ivy Anderson joins the act
summary: Ivy came with the band as a lively entertainer; the act was well rehearsed, and she played poker with the band on trains.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Right. Oh, I know what we haven't talked about. When Ivy came with the band. Ivy was with the band when you played the Palladium, wasn't she? Or was she that first time? No, Well, maybe she wasn't.
We didn't have a singer, did we?
Well, then, I -- I can look that up, too,
because I'll look up Ivy here. But it seems to me that that was about the next thing. Ivy was playing at the Grand Terrace.
And Earl was doing the show, and Ivy was a soubrette or something.
And you were playing the theater?
The band was doing -- and you had a terrific show.
And I guess Duke had never had a girl -- well, he had never had a singer at all, had he?
When did Herb Jeffries come with him?
Yes. I feel so. I believe so.

Well, let's talk about -- I did a piece on Ivy, and I remember her telling about when she -- when she went out with the band, when she came out on the stage at the Oriental, how scared she was. And she was so scared she wasn't going over very well. And then Sonny started shouting from the drums, and the people all laughed and she relaxed and everything happened, you know, and it all came off beautifully. And that really established it, didn't it?
Because -- I mean, Ivy was always -- in a sense, wouldn't you say it was like an act? Ivy coming on with the band was, in a sense, like an act. I mean, she came on -- there was humor.
And there was good humor and humor -- I mean, she didn't come on singing a ballad.
No. She was a great entertainer.
Or it wasn't romance and this and that. But it was a gay thing where she and Duke worked off one another.
And so on. And then Sonny always got in that act.
Yeah. It was well planned, really. Well rehearsed.
Between Irving Mills and different producers and different things, they staged the thing properly.
So really what it meant was that the act, the band, in theaters, changed to the extent that it closed with the girl singer, didn't it?
I don't remember how it closed.
Maybe she just came on at the end.
And did her three numbers, or maybe four -- came back and did a fourth.
-- came on with their thing. Yeah. That's
right. Well, what did it seem like, with a gal starting to travel with the band? That was --
She even played cards, do you recall?
Yeah. She fit right in. Played poker with us on the train.
We'd set up and she'd be right there playing poker. Yeah.
Isn't that funny? Well, then, Ivy was with the band for a long time.
What, about ten years, I think, wasn't it?
Yeah. I think so too. Did Ivy quit because she got sick, or did she quit because she really wanted to settle down on the West Coast? Do you remember?
I wasn't there when she left.
